correctness.rationale: For fixed n>=5 with all b_i>0, the precise closure S-epsilon=sin(sum_i arcsin(b_i t))/t (t=(2R)^-1) has removable analytic singularity; its even Taylor series is S-H*t^2/6+O(t^4), H=S^3-sum b_i^3>0. Inverting v=t^2 proves R=sqrt(H/(24 epsilon))(1+O(epsilon)), R^-2 derivative 24/H. The oriented fan area [sum sin(2arcsin b_i t)-sin(2 sum arcsin b_i t)]/(8t^2)=H*t/6+O(t^3) gives A=sqrt(H epsilon/6)(1+O(epsilon)) and A^2 derivative H/6. Exact chord-coordinate trigonometric expressions yield x_j=u_j+O(epsilon), y_j/sqrt(epsilon)=sqrt(6/H)*u_j(S-u_j)+O(epsilon). The fixed-n Hausdorff limit is the *polygonal chain through* sampled parabola points, not the smooth parabolic arc. Classical uniqueness identifies the analytic small-slack branch; no global-in-epsilon conclusion. Inspected check.py evaluates six short-side arrays with root-finding, not proof for all n.
